title: Quantum Natural Gradient on Quotient Spaces
abstract: Parametrized quantum circuits often contain state-preserving redundancies that make the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) singular even when the physical state manifold is regular. We formulate quantum natural gradient (QNG) on the resulting parameter quotient and prove that, when the prescribed redundancy exhausts the Fisher kernel, the Moore--Penrose update is the minimum-norm horizontal lift of the quotient Riemannian gradient. A circuit-to-orbit transfer principle separates intrinsic state distinguishability from circuit-coordinate distortion and gives the exact condition under which a circuit realizes an intrinsic orbit-QNG direction. Representation theory then yields root-resolved Fisher scales on highest-weight flag orbits and isotropic intrinsic metrics for Slater and fermionic-Gaussian manifolds. On cominuscule embeddings, intrinsic fidelity QNG conserves principal-defect ratios and reduces to one scalar equation; Lie-retracted steps are locally cubic at $η=2$, with stability boundary $η=4$. For finite-shot implementations, we separate exact gauge removal from regularization of physical soft modes, obtain zero cumulative gauge drift under structural projection, and derive confidence-controlled soft-mode rules. Under depolarization, inverse-Fisher scaling restores deterministic scale only by amplifying fluctuations and therefore cannot recover a lost update signal-to-noise ratio. A redundant Slater/Givens circuit verifies the transfer law and the predicted finite-shot tradeoffs.
summary: This theoretical paper develops the Quantum Natural Gradient (QNG) framework for quantum circuits suffering from parameter redundancies. It mathematically proves how to correctly compute the gradient on the resulting quotient space, providing a robust optimization tool. This is vital for designing stable and accurate variational quantum algorithms by separating true physical distinguishability from parametrization artifacts.
main_problem: The paper addresses the mathematical challenge of defining and optimizing Quantum Natural Gradient (QNG) when the parameterization of a quantum state is redundant, leading to a singular Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM).
main_result: It proves that the Moore--Penrose update correctly implements the minimum-norm horizontal lift of the quotient Riemannian gradient under specific conditions of redundancy exhaustion.
method: The methodology involves formulating the problem on the parameter quotient space, utilizing representation theory, and developing a 'circuit-to-orbit transfer principle' to separate intrinsic state distinguishability from circuit-coordinate distortion.
model_or_system: The model involves parametrized quantum circuits, $ho(	heta) = U(	heta)ho_0U(	heta)^\dagger$, used in variational quantum algorithms to prepare quantum states.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM), intrinsic orbit Fisher operator, principal-defect ratios, and finite-shot resource-accuracy tradeoffs.
important_parameters: Learning rate ($\eta$), noise scaling ($s$), and the structure of the redundancy group ($\Gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a smooth state map into the orbit and relies on local differentiability and spectral gap conditions for convergence proofs.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining QNG on quotient spaces to establishing the mathematical equivalence between the pseudoinverse update and the true quotient gradient. It then applies this framework to specific physical scenarios (e.g., flag orbits) and concludes with rigorous analyses of finite-shot noise and gauge removal.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, coordinate-independent mathematical framework for optimizing quantum circuits, which is crucial for developing robust quantum machine learning algorithms that can handle physical symmetries and redundancies.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Circuit-to-orbit Fisher transfer in the redundant Slater/Givens circuit. The intrinsic real-Grassmann Fisher operator is isotropic, while the gate-coordinate QFIM has condition number 356.548. The factorization F = BTB has relative error 1.273 × 10−10, and the exact pseudoinverse update induces the intrinsic real-Grassmann gradient to angular error 1.207 × 10−6

FIG. 2. Equal-total-shot comparison for ambient and quotient estimators. Curves show medians and interquartile ranges over 64 replicates. Structural projection eliminates gauge displacement, while quotient-only estimation spends the fixed budget on the smaller physical block.

FIG. 3. Exact-gauge and physical-soft-mode tradeoff under continuous release. Six candidate directions acquire physical Fisher weight while six known exact gauge directions remain redundant. Hard projection becomes biased after release, whereas the gauge-calibrated anisotropic rule retains candidate motion and eliminates displacement in the known gauge block. The plotted rule is the low-cost gauge-noise proxy motivated by theorem V.15; theorem V.16 supplies the corresponding independent-pilot, confidence-certified scalar alternative.
